title: Durable Functions: Long-Running Workflows
description: Build long-running, stateful workflows with Durable Functions using orchestrations, activities, and sub-orchestrations.

data.text: Durable Functions is an extension of Azure Functions that lets you write stateful workflows in code. It manages state, checkpoints, and restarts automatically, so you can build long-running processes without managing infrastructure.

items: Orchestrator function — defines the workflow logic and order of steps
Activity function — performs a single unit of work (like a task step)
Entity function — manages state for small, independently updatable pieces of data
Client function — starts a new orchestration

data.caption: Durable Functions orchestration pattern
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    C[Client] -->|Start Orchestration| O[Orchestrator Function]
    O -->|Call| A1[Activity: Validate]
    O -->|Call| A2[Activity: Process]
    O -->|Call| A3[Activity: Notify]
    A1 -->|Result| O
    A2 -->|Result| O
    A3 -->|Result| O
    O -->|Final Result| C

data.title: C# — Orchestrator and Activity Functions
Deterministic Code
data.text: Orchestrator code must be deterministic — no DateTime.UtcNow, no GUIDs, no random numbers outside activity functions. Durable Functions replays the orchestrator to rebuild state, so non-deterministic code causes errors.

rows: Run tasks in parallel, aggregate results
Periodically check until a condition is met

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Durable Functions manage state and checkpoints automatically
Orchestrators define the workflow; activities do the work
Common patterns include chaining, fan-out, and async HTTP APIs
data.takeaway: Durable Functions let you build reliable, long-running workflows without managing state manually.
